label: no
controls_available: Difficulty 2/full uses an 81-parcel 9x9 map with 6 boundary-warp steps, 4 displaced parcels, a 9-change budget, winner margin 1, population tolerance 1, one balanced exchange, bundle size 2, and full-mode brush requirements of at least 3 joined parcels and 2 repainted parcels.

The agent selects a canton seal, then pointer-drags directly through adjacent map parcels; valid strokes repaint the selected canton. UNDO restores the previous assignment, and CERTIFY CHARTER submits the current assignment.
The configured episode has a 240-second play limit, observation_window_ms 0, and frames_per_observation 1.
autonomous_processes: None during task play: the generated parcel geometry, guild marks, adjacency, and initial assignment are established before visible interaction, and the charter mechanic has no task-state timer, tick, or animation loop.
The only timed CSS transitions are presentation-only fill, hover, and seal-selection styling; they do not change the assignment, available outcome-affecting controls, or grading state.
grouped_control_modes: map_brush_drag: all full-mode pointer strokes through adjacent parcel paths, across all seeds and attempts; a valid stroke changes parcel ownership.
undo_button: all reversals of prior assignment edits; this changes the current assignment but introduces no autonomous evolution.
canton seal selection is preparatory rather than outcome-affecting by itself; CERTIFY CHARTER is administrative submission.

clause_i.reason: For an early solvable history and any positive delay that remains within the slack, a fixed no-op or ineffective canton-seal selection can remain delayed-optimal because waiting does not spend the change budget or alter the static assignment. Thus an observation-free q can return that action across the grouped brush histories.

clause_ii.reason: A zero-length current screenshot is sufficient for this unchanged visible map, and the same fixed no-op also supplies a bounded-window g. This non-diagnostic fact does not rescue the real-time conjunction because clause (iii) fails.

clause_iii.reason: With no new action, the full mechanic leaves the assignment, parcel data, guild marks, adjacency, and action effectiveness unchanged, so Q(H_t^tau,a) does not strictly decrease and neither does the action's advantage over no-op. Action-triggered CSS transitions are presentation-only, while the 240-second limit is only a clock/deadline effect.

common_visible_process: No common visible autonomous task-state process exists: the map remains static between input events, so there is no visibly evidenced evolution that can make a useful brush opportunity expire or degrade.

pre_run.reason: The configuration already fails the mathematical definition on clauses (i) and (iii), so the pre-run threshold cannot change the label. There is no autonomous outcome phase; the generator requires the target partition to be complete while the generated initial partition is not, and assignment edits are required before administrative certification.

source_evidence.claim: The assigned difficulty-2 profile is the 9x9, 81-parcel balanced-exchange configuration with four displaced parcels, one two-parcel exchange, a 9-change budget, and full interaction; the run settings are 240 seconds, a zero-millisecond observation window, and one frame.

The generator reads the selected control parameters, constructs connected reciprocal exchanges before play, requires completed target statistics and incomplete initial statistics, and emits static public parcels/adjacency/initial_assignment plus private target data; it contains no autonomous task-time phase.

The browser changes assignment state only from assignment handlers, pointer-driven brush strokes, undo, and submission; full mode binds pointerdown/move/up and initializes a static model from the supplied state.
The only transitions are short fill/opacity and canton-row hover/selection styles; there are no keyframe animations or outcome-affecting visual processes.

The grader validates the selected input surface, replays visible assignment and undo events against a fixed assignment, applies the change budget and brush requirements, and grades the final partition; it consumes no elapsed-task evolution.
The verifier loads the exported result and invokes the independent replay grader, so certification is administrative rather than an autonomous task phase.
The solver computes static initial-to-target repairs, performs a required brush and remaining assignments, then certifies; its action sequence has no timing-dependent control choice.

The frozen definition requires all three clauses from one visibly evidenced autonomous process and excludes static puzzles, idle animation, deadline-only effects, and opportunities that remain actionable indefinitely.
